title: Assessment Administration Coordinator
description:
Assessment Administration Coordinator

Location: Nominal office of York, with expected minimum attendance of once per month
Salary: £27,010 gross per annum
Contract: Full Time, Permanent

Applications close on 14th September at 9am. Interviews will take place via MS Teams w/c 28th September

Benefits:
- A generous pension plan with USS
- Enhanced family leave benefits
- 31 days annual leave, plus bank holidays
- Flexible working hours
- Hybrid work
- Employee Assistance Programme access
- Personal Financial Wellbeing advice access

to name a few

The Role:

We are looking for an Assessment Administration Coordinator to support the delivery of a range of prestigious peer review and assessment services across the higher education sector.

This role will provide end-to-end administrative support for either institutional services (including Athena Swan, Race Equality Charter, Inclusive Institutions Framework, Impact Awards and Accreditation) or individual services (including Fellowship, End-Point Assessment and Awards).

You will play a vital role in ensuring assessment processes run smoothly, efficiently and accurately, supporting applicants, reviewers, institutions and subject experts throughout the assessment journey.

Working within a collaborative team, you will help deliver excellent customer experiences while contributing to ongoing service improvements and transformation projects.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys coordinating multiple priorities and has a strong commitment to quality, accuracy and continuous improvement.

There are 3 opportunities available for this role, 1 permanent position within Institutional Services and 2 Fixed Term Contracts within Individual Services.

Job requirements
- Experience delivering high-quality administrative support within education or a related professional environment.
- Proven experience delivering excellent customer service and handling customer enquiries and complaints.
- Experience working with databases, CRM systems and case management systems.
- Experience using multiple digital systems to record, manage and monitor data accurately.
- Experience supporting external customers and stakeholders at varying levels of seniority.
- Knowledge and experience of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
- Experience managing confidential and sensitive information appropriately.

Job responsibilities

Assessment Process Administration
- Support the effective administration of end-to-end peer review assessment processes across both institutional and individual services.
- Conduct initial quality assurance checks on applications to ensure eligibility requirements and submission standards are met prior to review.
- Coordinate assessment activities and ensure results are released accurately and within published timescales.
- Provide administrative support for assessment panels, peer review meetings and reviewer activities.
- Prepare, issue and manage assessment outcomes, feedback documentation and certification for successful applicants.
- Maintain accurate records and data throughout the assessment lifecycle in accordance with compliance requirements and service standards.
- Support the administration of peer reviewers, consultants and other associates involved in assessment delivery.

Customer Service and Stakeholder Support
- Respond to application and post-recognition enquiries in a timely, professional and customer-focused manner.
- Escalate complex issues appropriately while maintaining a positive customer experience.
- Build strong working relationships with institutional contacts, contract holders, programme leaders, programme administrators and subject expert teams.
- Support a seamless customer and member experience across all assessment services.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of products, services, systems and processes to provide accurate guidance and support.

Data Management and Reporting
- Maintain and monitor information within databases, CRM systems and assessment platforms.
- Produce reports and administrative data to support operational monitoring and service delivery.
- Support annual HESA and international data returns where applicable.
- Ensure all records are accurate, secure and compliant with GDPR and organisational policies.

Continuous Improvement and Transformation
- Contribute ideas to improve administrative efficiency and enhance customer experiences.
- Support assessment delivery transformation projects, including system testing, piloting and process improvements.
- Actively contribute to a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.
- Keep process documentation up to date and support the implementation of new systems and ways of working.

Compliance and Governance
- Ensure policies, procedures and regulatory requirements are consistently followed.
- Uphold organisational commitments relating to equality, diversity and inclusion, data protection, health and safety and charity governance.
- Handle sensitive and confidential information with professionalism and discretion.

What you'll get

You'll have the opportunity to shape how finance supports the organisation, influence decision-making at all levels, and lead a team committed to delivering an excellent service. In return, you'll join a collaborative and values-driven organisation where your expertise, leadership and ideas will make a real difference.

If you're an experienced finance professional who combines strong operational leadership with a passion for developing people and improving processes, we'd love to hear from you.

Advance HE is a member-led, sector-owned charity that works with institutions and higher education across the world to improve higher education for staff, students and society.

Our strategic priorities of: maximising membership impact and value, supporting leadership, management and governance development for transformational change and developing educational excellence for the higher education of the future supports the work of our members and the sector.

It is our people and the people we help that really make us who we are!

To apply:

If you have the skills and experience required for this role, please click on Apply today to be taken to our site to complete your application.

Advance HE is committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of their background.

No agencies please.

title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator

Knaresborough, North Yorkshire
£26,000 to £30,000 depending on experience
Full-time, Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week, fully office based

Benefits: Generous annual bonus scheme, 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, additional annual leave with length of service, private medical insurance, life assurance, income protection, enhanced employer pension contribution, enhanced maternity and paternity pay, employee discounts and lifestyle benefits platform, wellbeing support services, two paid volunteering days per year, ClassPass credits, ongoing training and development and genuine opportunities for career progression.

This is a newly created role within a rapidly growing organisation, offering an excellent opportunity to join an expanding HR function and work closely with an experienced Head of HR.

With wide exposure across HR, this role offers plenty of variety and the chance to make the position your own as it evolves. You'll receive ongoing training and development, making it ideal for an experienced HR Administrator or someone looking to build a long-term career within HR in a supportive and forward-thinking business.

HR Administrator Key Responsibilities:
- Coordinating recruitment activities, including arranging interviews and liaising with candidates, hiring managers and recruitment partners
- Preparing employment contracts, offer letters and right-to-work documentation
- Supporting onboarding and offboarding processes
- Maintaining accurate employee records and HR systems
- Assisting with payroll and employee benefits administration
- Responding to employee queries and providing day-to-day HR support
- Supporting HR projects and continuous improvement initiatives
- Working collaboratively with teams across the business to ensure HR processes run smoothly

Candidate Requirements:
- Previous HR administration experience would be advantageous, although we would also welcome applications from candidates with strong administrative experience and a genuine interest in pursuing a career in HR
- Excellent organisational skills with strong attention to detail
- Able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines effectively
- Professional, discreet and comfortable handling confidential information
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
- Confident using Microsoft Office and learning new systems
- Proactive, positive and keen to develop professionally

To Apply

Please submit your CV via the link or contact Beth Davies at Unity Resourcing for more information.

title: Administrator - Receptionist
company: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
description: An opportunity has arisen for a fixed term 6 month position to work in the reception of Hummingbird house, home to the Harrogate & Ripon Community Treatment team. Hummingbird House accommodates Adult Mental Health teams and CAMHS, the opportunity is within the adult reception team. Hummingbird House is situated in the centre of Harrogate Town, a short walk from local shops and amenities, as well as being located close to the central bus terminal and train station. As a member of our Hummingbird House reception team you will be the first point of contact for patients, families, and visitors, you will play a vital role in creating a welcoming and supportive environment at the heart of the hospital. This is an opportunity to make a real difference by proving both practical assistance and a kind reassuring presence. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. The main duties will require you to greet service users, carers, and external partners face to face including answering queries via telephone in a professional and friendly manner. The role will involve managing incoming and outgoing post, room bookings, ordering supplies, logging calls with estates, dealing with prescriptions, petty cash, booking taxis or patient transport, arranging collection of pathology samples, and general office duties. The ability to remain calm, communicate clearly, adhere to confidentiality, and promote a positive culture for those living with mental health issues and/or learning disabilities. The successful candidate will be expected to perform basic admin tasks, update clinic lists, maintain visitor logs, issue access cards, deal with incoming & outgoing post, photocopying and ensure that all information in the reception area for staff and the public is clearly displayed and updated as appropriate. For more details, please read carefully the job description, to be successful at shortlisting please briefly describe how you match this description citing examples to reinforce your experience. Our Trust is dedicated to supporting our colleagues in providing an excellent working environment and encourages everyone to share their progressive ideas. All staff have regular 1-2-1 supervisions and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for celebration of achievements, and discussions around challenges, and your aspirations. You will be required to work 7.5 hours shifts.. You will be fully supported by a welcoming team of admin and clinical staff and will not be lone working on the premises at any time. If successful you will be supplied with a job plan and a fully supported induction. For an informal discussion or to arrange a visit to Hummingbird House please contact Poppy Danahay, Team Manager - poppy.danahay@nhs.net 01423 852000 This is a rewarding role working in a desirable team, if you feel this is the challenge for you then we very much look forward to receiving your application. Please refer to the attached job description and person specification for further detailed information to ensure that you meet the role criteria before applying. This job advert may close early if a high volume of applications have been received. If interested, please apply for this post as soon as possible.

title: Team Administrator
company: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
description: A rare opportunity has arisen for a dedicated and experienced administrator to join our friendly team based at Alexander House. Our team provides essential compassionate mental health support and care to our older people in the local area and is situated in the beautiful and historical market town of Knaresborough. Alexander House is just a short 10-minute walk to local amenities and has free onsite parking. As an essential part of the community/memory team, you will be based in the admin office and be supported by our existing welcoming administrators to work closely with the clinical staff in delivering our Trust mission of co-creating a great experience for our patients, carers, and families. If you are an individual with experience working in a busy office environment, who is confident in using IT systems including Outlook for effective diary management. Someone who thrives in a dynamic busy setting and is keen to join a team striving to make a real difference in your local community then we are looking for you. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. Whilst having previous experience in an administrative role is essential, NHS or other health care experience is not. We are first and foremost looking for a colleague with a passion for helping people who believes in delivering excellent customer service, who has a keen interest in learning and working in a health care setting with a 'can do' attitude. This role is at the heart of the multi-disciplinary team which means you will work closely with nurses, healthcare professionals, consultants, and management to ensure that they have everything admin wise they need to provide the best possible care to our patients. We are looking for someone who is comfortable multitasking, someone who can communicate confidently, build strong working relationships with a variety of people, who can prioritise their workload and who is genuinely interested in understanding and supporting the challenges that mental health care provides. Your main duties will be processing referrals to the team, booking assessment and treatment appointments, liaising with patients, carers and other stakeholders, typing letters and maintaining accurate, confidential patient records. For more details, please read carefully the job description, to be successful at shortlisting please briefly describe how you match this description citing examples to reinforce your experience. If you do not have maths or English to the required standard please state your intention to work towards. Our Trust is dedicated to supporting our colleagues in providing an excellent working environment and encourages everyone to share their progressive ideas. All staff have regular 1-2-1 supervisions and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for celebration of achievements, and discussions around challenges, and your aspirations. You will work alongside other team administrators and our senior administrators (medical secretaries) to deliver admin support. As a valuable member of the team, you will be invited to attend regular meetings to improve your knowledge and understanding of the services, you will also be required to minute meetings and keep accurate records. If successful, you will be supplied with a job plan and a fully supported induction. A visit to the team would be most welcome, should you wish to ask any specific questions or request a visit please contact the team manager (details below). This is a rewarding role working in a desirable team, if you feel this is the challenge for you then we very much look forward to receiving your application.
